question_text: Which regulatory circuits exhibit bistability or switch-like behaviour, and what evidence establishes the switch rather than a graded response?
cutoff_rationale: 5-point percentile-block title reading from p18 to p50 (decile bands were smooth, no visible cliff -- same as every question so far). 'Switch' is a heavily overloaded word: false positives from immunology (antibody class-switch recombination), chemistry (molecular switches), and optogenetics appear interleaved with genuine bistability content rather than cleanly separated the way glmp-q3's zone recovered. 5-point blocks stop having an on-topic majority around p27/p28 (score ~0.371-0.376) and never regain a clear majority afterward, though scattered genuine hits (phase variation, phenotypic switching) persist as late as ~p49. Cutoff set at that p27/p28 transition.
